---
title: "Redefining an existing function masks it without warning"
ref: FUN-05
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`2`, the mean"
versions: "All"
source: "safer-r, hadley/strict"

::: {.piege}
```{r}
mean <- function(...) {
  sum(...)
}
mean(c(1, 2, 3))
find("mean")
```
:::

## Why

R looks for a function first in the current environment, then in the attached packages, from the most recent to the oldest. A `mean` function created in the workspace therefore comes before the one in {base}, and R says nothing.

The same mechanism applies between packages. Loading {plyr} after {dplyr} replaces `summarise()` and `mutate()` with their {plyr} namesakes, which ignore `group_by()`. R does print a message when loading, but it is easy to miss, and `library(plyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)` or `suppressPackageStartupMessages()` remove even that one.

## The fix

Prefix with the package name whenever in doubt, remove the masking object, or use {conflicted}, which turns any ambiguity into an error.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
base::mean(c(1, 2, 3))
rm(mean)
mean(c(1, 2, 3))
```
:::
